Why This Transition Is a Gain — Not a Lateral Move
Professional Summary

I'm a customer support leader with 19+ years of hands-on experience across Technical Support Operations and Customer Experience — currently leading AMER business operations for Salesforce Field Service, with deep working fluency across Asset Service Management, Scheduling & Optimization, and Mobile Workforce Management — the three core deployment domains where enterprise Field Service success is won or lost.

I haven't held a formal PM title, but the work I've been doing for the past nearly 4 years has pulled me deep into product thinking. Supporting complex enterprise customers at scale means I've had to get comfortable living in the gap between what customers experience and what Engineering understands — translating messy, real-world pain into clear, actionable problem statements; identifying undocumented product gaps before they become larger systemic issues; and working closely with Engineering to challenge severity classifications and shape fix strategies that actually got adopted.

Beyond escalation response, I have proactively driven adoption at scale — running a structured outreach programme across a 1,435-account North America funnel, personally engaging 150+ accounts in collaboration with AEs, CSMs, Product, and Engineering to surface adoption blockers before they became support tickets. That kind of cross-functional engagement — spanning Account Executives, Engineering leads, Product managers, and Customer Success — is where I have spent nearly 4 years finding leverage.

I don't come from PM. I come from the customer. And I think that's a different kind of foundation — one built on listening first, not shipping first.

Bank of Nova Scotia · Case 473442710
$30M Renewal
SFS Scheduler — Aura/LWC · Engagement Channel Type Bug
My team identified the Select Service Appointment Time component was broken for customers using Engagement Channel Type without a Work Type Group ID. I challenged the P3 priority classification, escalated to engineering leadership via Sr Director TSE, and drove a dual-track fix strategy: interim LWC workaround in parallel with the permanent Aura fix. Fix: GUS W-22897038 → Release 262.9.2 + R2a Major Release (June 12–13).
✓ Customer confirmed out of impact · $30M renewal protected
Access TeleCare · Case 473087660
Red Account
SFS Global Optimization / Dynamic Scaling · Undocumented Product Behaviour
Dynamic Scaling was failing to assign Service Appointments due to a clustering issue. I identified a completely undocumented behaviour — the Custom Field Count Rule was causing Service Appointments to be skipped at end-of-day. Engineering agreed to update product documentation. Root fix confirmed on customer sandbox.
✓ Red Account officially closed
Southern California Edison · Cases 472696264 & 472907022
$6.8M · CEO Visibility
SFS Mobile iOS Offline Mode · $1B+ Wildfire Mitigation Coverage
SFS Mobile iOS was crashing on Pending Upload queue overflow — blocking InspectForce 2.0 go-live. I proactively treated a Sev2 as Sev1 urgency, identified two distinct engineering issues, formally documented SCE's performance testing requirements (40 survey forms, 3,000–4,000 records), and led a 5-hour joint customer call enabling go-live. Long-term fix delivered in Release 260.1 (GA: March 4, 2026).
✓ Go-live enabled · $6.8M secured · 90%+ performance improvement
Most PMs have to build a VoC feedback loop. I have been operating one — across three Sev1s, 150+ personally engaged accounts, and 15+ AE/CSM relationships — with receipts, metrics, and named outcomes.

The People Philosophy: A Leadership Identity That Scales Into Product
The operating system behind every team I have built

My leadership framework — Achievement · Balance · Connection · Diversity — is not a performance. It is the operating system behind the team culture and stakeholder relationships that made the escalation outcomes above possible.

A PM who leads with this philosophy builds the kind of team and customer trust that sustains high performance across release cycles. In a product that serves field workers doing time-critical, physically demanding, high-stakes work — this people-first orientation is a product advantage, not a soft benefit.

🏆
Achievement
Setting ambitious goals and holding the team accountable to outcomes — not effort. Every escalation above was driven by a clear definition of done.
⚖️
Balance
Sustaining high performance without burning out the team or the customer relationship. Long-term trust is built between the sprint crises, not during them.
🤝
Connection
Building genuine working relationships across Engineering, CSM, AE, and customers — the kind that get a Slack message answered at 11pm during a Sev1.
🌍
Diversity
Drawing on different perspectives to get to better answers faster. The undocumented product gaps I identified came from listening to signals others had filtered out.
